characterList.description: A male voice speaking during the video. He is not visible.
characterList.name: Jonathan Stark

content_metadata.description: This video provides a tutorial on creating a native iPhone app using the PhoneGap framework. Jonathan Stark guides the audience through the technical steps involved, including downloading PhoneGap, setting up the development environment, and customizing app elements.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the framework used to create the iPhone app?

qAndA.answer: The `info.plist` file controls the app name and icon.
qAndA.question: What file controls the app name and icon?

qAndA.answer: The white flash is caused by the startup screen image not being tall enough.
qAndA.question: What causes the white flash at the bottom of the startup screen?

qAndA.answer: The developer adjusts the screen height by changing the `min-height` property in the CSS file.
qAndA.question: How does the developer adjust the screen height to use the whole screen?

qAndA.answer: The `bundle identifier` needs to be set up appropriately for deployment to an actual device.
qAndA.question: What important identifier needs to be set up for deployment to an actual device?

activities.description: Building and running the app in the simulator.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The tutorial is relevant to developers interested in cross-platform mobile app development, offering insights into the practical aspects of using web technologies to create native applications.

narrativeProgression.description: Jonathan Stark introduces PhoneGap and initiates the download.
He demonstrates the web app in a browser before transforming it into a native application.
The iPhone simulator launches, displaying the initial version of the app.
He customizes the app's icon and startup screen.
He addresses screen size adjustments for optimal display.
He briefly touches upon the bundle identifier setup for deployment.

scenes.thematicElements: The scene revolves around the process of creating native mobile applications using web technologies. PhoneGap is highlighted as a tool for building applications that run on various mobile platforms.
scenes.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Using PhoneGap

climax.description: The climax occurs when the app has been customized and runs successfully on the simulator.

storylines.description: The storyline follows the creation of a native iPhone app from web technologies using PhoneGap.

content_metadata.title: Creating an iPhone App with PhoneGap

trimmingSuggestions.description: Trim the segment where Jonathan Stark repeatedly cleans and builds the project to maintain a higher dynamism.

youtube_description:
Quick overview of how to take a garden variety web app built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and convert it to a native iPhone app using PhoneGap.

In this example, I used jQTouch to style and animated the web app, but this would work with any web app or JavaScript framework. 

You can learn more about building iPhone apps with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript here:
http://building-iphone-apps.labs.oreilly.com/

Related links:
http://phonegap.com/
http://jqtouch.com/
http://jonathanstark.com/
http://oreilly.com/catalog/9780596805791
youtube_title: Build Native iPhone Apps with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PhoneGap
